method: For each previously identified radial band, sample RGB over 1440 angular positions, average RGB along radius, compute centered angular RGB-difference magnitude, then independently search one uniform k-fold phase maximizing mean boundary response. Report percentile rank of each predicted boundary against the full angular response distribution. No target cell count is inferred from this test.

bands.interpretation: 3-fold family has two high-response axes but the third is weak/ambiguous. 3-fold periodicity remains candidate/partial rather than a verified three-cell partition.

All seven predicted axes land above approximately the 76th percentile; five are above approximately the 82nd percentile and four above the 95th percentile. This is substantial local support for a seven-fold boundary family, but not yet proof of seven closed cells.

All twelve predicted axes are high-response locations; eleven exceed approximately the 96th percentile and the weakest remains approximately the 88th percentile. Strong local support exists for a 12-fold boundary family.

h22.reason: Independent band periodicity plus local phase/axis continuity strongly supports 7-fold and 12-fold structures and partially supports 3-fold structure. This still does not establish exactly 3+7+12 closed cells.

nextGate: Build wedge/cell interior evidence between adjacent predicted boundaries, test radial closure at the measured band limits, and infer actual planar cells. Do not promote CR-MF or AK until closed-region topology is stable across sensitivity settings.
